title: Why You Can't Tickle Yourself
hook: Your own fingers are the one thing that cannot surprise you. Here is why.
description: A short why-it-happens explainer about why self-tickling never lands.

scenes.vo: Try it right now. Reach over and tickle your own arm. Almost nothing.
scenes.caption: Reach over and tickle your own arm. Nothing.
scenes.whyArt: wide shot of a person reaching for their own arm

scenes.vo: The guess is that you are just not sensitive there. You are. Ask a friend.
scenes.caption: The guess says you are not sensitive there.

scenes.vo: The real reason is smaller. Your brain predicts the touch before it lands.
scenes.caption: Your brain predicts the touch before it lands.
scenes.whyArt: close-in diagram of the prediction signal

scenes.vo: Test it: a robot hand that tickles with a half-second delay works instantly.
scenes.caption: Add a delay and suddenly it works.
scenes.whyArt: worked-example panel with a delayed robot hand

scenes.vo: So it is not the finger. It is a brain that cannot surprise itself.
scenes.caption: A brain that cannot surprise itself.
scenes.whyArt: comparison: self touch vs delayed touch
